verdict.rationale: Bitwarden documents its own desktop apps: the passkey docs say vault items can be autofilled from "desktop apps". Community posts confirm a desktop client exists, citing a redesigned desktop/autofill UX and requests for Linux biometric unlock. TOTP generation is documented generally, but nothing shows the desktop app itself displaying codes. A user also reports the desktop UX became bloated and slower, which lowers quality but does not contradict the capability. missing for 10: explicit docs that the desktop app generates and shows TOTP codes, dedicated desktop app documentation (platforms, vault browsing and editing), hands-on corroboration of desktop vault and code access.

support.subject: As a power user, a first-class desktop app gives me codes and vault access on my computer, not just on mobile

citations.quote: Save passkeys in your Bitwarden vault and use the browser extension, mobile apps, or desktop apps to autofill them across the apps and websites you use every day.
it automatically produces the time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs), six-digit codes using SHA-1 that rotate every 30 seconds
A user says the desktop/autofill UX was redesigned last year into something bloated, full of whitespace and slower.
